instrument_name: Wis. Stat. ch. 104 Minimum Wage Law (published 10-1-26)
figure_or_rule_carried: 104.035(1)(a) minimum wage 7.25/h; minor 7.25; opportunity employee (under 20, first 90 days) 5.90; meal/lodging allowances lodging 58/week or 8.30/day, meals 87/week or 4.15/meal. 104.001(2): no city, village, town or county may enact a minimum wage ordinance (local minimum wages void since 2005-06-16). 104.09 records of names, addresses, hours and wages. No scheduled 2026/2027 increase in the text published 2026-10-01 (updated through 2025 Wis. Act 247).

instrument_name: Wis. Admin. Code ch. DWD 272 Minimum Wages (Register November 2024 No. 827)
figure_or_rule_carried: 272.03(1): 7.25 all/minor, 5.90 opportunity employee (not yet 20, first 90 consecutive days). 272.03(2) tipped: cash wage 2.33/h (opportunity 2.13/h); tip credit only with a tip declaration signed each pay period and payroll records showing tips plus wages reach the minimum weekly. 272.10 pay statement: hours worked, rate of pay, amount and reason of each deduction (coding allowed). 272.11 payroll records kept at least 3 years: name, address, date of birth, hire/leave dates, daily start/stop, meal periods, daily/weekly hours, rate and wages per pay period, each deduction, output if not time-paid.

instrument_name: Wis. Admin. Code ch. DWD 274 Hours of Work and Overtime (Register November 2003 No. 575)
figure_or_rule_carried: 274.03: time and one-half the regular rate for hours over 40 per week (no daily overtime). 274.04 exemptions interpreted consistently with FLSA (EAP etc.). 274.015: domestic service in a household by a household not covered. 274.06: records kept at least 3 years.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. ch. 109 Wage Payments, Claims and Collections (published 6-25-25)
figure_or_rule_carried: 109.03(1): pay at least monthly all wages earned to a day not more than 31 days before payment (logging and farm labor at least quarterly; CBA, school and comp-time exceptions). 109.03(2): an employee who quits or is discharged is paid in full no later than the next regular payday or the 31-day limit, whichever is earlier (commission sales agents and written definite-term contracts excepted). 109.01(1r): officers, directors, managerial/executive/commissioned sales and confidential employees excluded from 'employee'. 109.07: 60 days notice of business closing/mass layoff (employers of 50+ in WI). Edition read is 6-25-25; 10-1-26 edition not re-fetched.

instrument_name: Wisconsin DWD Equal Rights - Wage Payment and Collection page and FAQ
article_or_section: Direct Deposit Wage Payments; FAQ vacation/PTO
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer may require direct deposit at no cost to the employee; the employee must still receive a stub showing rate of pay, hours worked and the amount and reason of each deduction. Separated employees are paid on the regular schedule. Unused vacation/PTO at separation: payable if a written vacation policy exists without a written forfeiture policy; employers are not required to provide vacation, holiday or sick pay.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. 103.10 Family or medical leave; 103.11; 103.12 local benefit preemption (published 10-1-26)
figure_or_rule_carried: WFMLA: employers with 50+ permanent employees; employee 52 consecutive weeks and 1,000 hours; family leave max 6 weeks birth/adoption, 2 weeks care of family member, 8 weeks combined; medical leave max 2 weeks per 12 months; leave unpaid (5)(a), employee may substitute paid or unpaid employer leave (5)(b). 103.10(1m): no city/village/town/county may require paid or unpaid leave; 103.12: no local ordinance may require employment benefits (ordinances in effect 2018-04-18 void). Hence no state or local paid sick leave mandate.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. 103.455 deductions for faulty workmanship, loss, theft or damage; 103.13 records (published 10-1-26)
figure_or_rule_carried: No deduction for defective work, lost/stolen property or damage unless written employee authorization, joint determination with employee representative, or court finding; unlawful deduction = liability for twice the amount. 103.13: employee may inspect personnel records at least twice per calendar year.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. ch. 812 subch. II Garnishment of earnings (published 10-1-26)
figure_or_rule_carried: 812.34(2)(a): 80% of disposable earnings exempt (max garnishment 20%, stricter than CCPA 25%); totally exempt if household income below poverty line or need-based assistance; garnishment limited so household income stays above the poverty line. Exemptions do not apply to support, unpaid taxes or bankruptcy orders. 812.33: garnishee (employer) fee 15 plus 3 for each payment after the first, deducted from amounts paid to the creditor. 812.43: no fee or adverse action against the debtor.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. 767.75 Assignment of income for payment obligations; 767.57(1e) (published 10-1-26)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer withholds from money paid later than one week after receipt of the notice of assignment and sends it within 5 days after the payday to the department or its designee; amount may not exceed 15 USC 1673(b)(2) limits; employer may keep its necessary disbursements not exceeding 3 per payment, deducted from the money paid to the payer; support assignment has priority over any other assignment, garnishment or similar process under state law. 767.57(1e): annual receiving and disbursing fee 65 withheld from income with the support.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. ch. 71 Income and franchise taxes (published 10-1-26): 71.06 rates; 71.63-71.67 withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: Assessment rates for taxable years after 2024: single/HoH 3.50% to 14,680; 4.40% to 50,480; 5.30% to 323,290; 7.65% above; joint 19,580 / 67,300 / 431,060; separate 9,790 / 33,650. From taxable years after 2025 bracket limits indexed by Aug CPI-U vs Aug 2024, rounded to 10. 71.64(1): employer withholds per DOR tables (other method needs DOR permission). 71.63: wages exclude agricultural labor and domestic service (among others); employee = resident anywhere or nonresident working in WI; corporate officers included. 71.65(1): wage statements to employees by January 31. NOTE: withholding tables (W-166 1/26) still use 3.54/4.65/5.30/7.65 at 12,760/25,520/280,950, not aligned to the 2025+ assessment rates (withholding approximates; reconciled on the return). IRC conformity located: as amended to 2022-12-31 for years after 2022 (corporate/franchise definitions read; individual 71.01(6) paragraph not isolated).

instrument_name: Wisconsin Publication W-166 Withholding Tax Guide (1/26): deposits, reconciliation, nonresidents, alternate-method examples
figure_or_rule_carried: Filing frequency assigned by DOR (annual/quarterly/monthly/semi-monthly; no dollar thresholds published), changed from 1 January on written notice. WT-6 deposit report: monthly/quarterly due last day of following month; semi-monthly: pay dates 1-15 due last day of month, 16-end due 15th of next month; filed even with zero; electronic unless waiver; ACH debit by 4:00 p.m. CST on due date. WT-7 annual reconciliation and W-2/1099 due January 31 (30 days after account closure); WT-7 rejected until all WT-6 filed. WT-4 exempt claim renewed annually by April 30; no WT-4 = zero exemptions. Nonresident exceptions: interstate carriers, reciprocity (IL, IN, KY, MI; W-220), air carriers 50% rule, expected WI earnings under 1,500, military spouse (W-221). Residents working outside WI: withholding on all wages; Minnesota special arrangement. HSA conformity from 2011. Third-party sick pay: third party reports and remits WI tax. Pension withholding on request, minimum 5 per payment. Agricultural/domestic exempt wages still reported on W-2 (state ID 036888888888801 if no WI account). Oracle: alternate-method worked examples 1-3 (weekly 350/1 ex -> 7.59; weekly 500/3 ex -> 14.34; married biweekly 1,000/3 ex -> 22.08). Construction misclassification fine 25,000.

instrument_name: Wisconsin Publication 117 Guide to Wisconsin Wage Statements and Information Returns (01/26)
article_or_section: 2 Chart 1; 3 Chart 2; 4 How to file; 5 Electronic specifications; 6 CF/SF
figure_or_rule_carried: Covers 2025 W-2s filed in 2026. W-2 due January 31 to DOR and employee (on last payment if employment ends). 10 or more wage statements (or 10+ of one information-return type) must be filed electronically: approved payroll software, keyed in My Tax Account, EFW2 file upload (W-2), IRS Pub 1220 file (1099). Specifications in Publication 172; no transmittal. CF/SF does not relieve 1099s carrying WI withholding. 15-digit WI withholding number; 036888888888801 when never held. Copies to recipient may truncate SSN; copies to DOR may not.

instrument_name: Wisconsin UI Employer Handbook UCB-201-P (R. 03/16/2026): coverage, exclusions, quarterly wage reporting, new hire, benefit reports
article_or_section: Section 1 Parts 2,5; Section 2 Parts 1-2; Section 4; Section 5
figure_or_rule_carried: Coverage: commercial employer 1+ employee in 20 weeks or 1,500 wages in a quarter; agricultural 20,000 cash wages in a quarter or 10+ workers in 20 weeks; domestic 1,000 cash wages in a quarter; 501(c)(3) 4+ in 20 weeks. Elective exclusion of principal corporate officers (25%+ ownership; 108.02(15)(L)). Quarterly contribution and wage report due by end of month after quarter, filed even with no payroll; 25+ employees must file electronically (s.108.205(2)), penalty 20 per employee if paper; late wage report 50 (within 30 days) or greater of 100 or 20 per employee. File formats: DWD layouts incl. modified IRS/SSA E/S record format. Required benefit reports UCB-16 Separation Notice, UCB-23, UCB-719 (respond when DWD requests; no separation notice to employee required by handbook). Poster UCB-7-P required. New hire: within 20 days of start, via wi-newhire.com (key or file), SFTP or paper (WT-4/W-4/list); fields employee name, address, SSN, date of birth, employer name, payroll address, FEIN, date of hire; multistate employers may choose one state.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. ch. 108 Unemployment Insurance and Reserves (published 10-1-26)
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable payroll: first 14,000 of wages per employee per calendar year for years after 2012 (fixed in statute, not indexed; rises automatically only if FUTA wage base exceeds it). Experience rate schedules A-D selected by fund cash balance on preceding June 30 (Schedule D at 1.2 billion+); Schedule D contribution rates from 0.00 (reserve 10%+) to 10.70 (overdrawn 9%+), solvency rates added separately; year-over-year rate increase capped at +1 point (reserve >= 0) or +2 points (negative reserve). 108.205(2) electronic wage reporting for 25+ employees.

instrument_name: Wisconsin DOR Publication 172 (1/26) Annual W-2, W-2C, 1099 and W-2G Electronic Reporting
article_or_section: Special notice; What's new; Common questions A-D; record layouts
figure_or_rule_carried: W-2 electronic format = SSA EFW2 (Pub 42-007, tax year 2025) with the state 'RS' record; W-2C = EFW2C (Pub 42-014); 1099/W-2G = IRS Pub 1220. State code in RS positions 3-4 and 274-275 (WI = 55). Same withholding tax account number on all W-2s. 10+ W-2s or 10+ of one information-return type: electronic mandatory. Tax-year-2025 W-2s and information returns due February 2, 2026; 30-day extension on good cause; no transmittal letter; test file optional (Data File Transfer page, immediate validation); sFTP accepted; no CD/flash/PDF media.

instrument_name: Wisconsin DOR Withholding Tax Update 2026-1 (October 2026), laws enacted as of 2026-10-30
article_or_section: W-2 wage reporting differences for 2026; Withholding tax rates; Agricultural labor; Pensions; Electronic filing mandate; PSP notice; Transportation fringe 2026-2027; WT-4 copies; Lock-in letters
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding rates: no plans to change; current rates remain those in W-166 (effective for periods on or after 2022-01-01). 2026 W-2 box 16 WI wages may differ from federal for IRC 112 (hazardous duty), 127 (student-loan payments), 128 (employer contributions to Trump accounts), 129 (dependent care above WI exemption), 132 (moving/bicycle) - WI does not follow P.L. 115-97 / 119-21 changes there. Agricultural labor (incl. H-2A) not wages under 71.63(6)(b): no withholding required, voluntary by agreement; W-2 if 600+ or any withholding. Pensions not wages: withhold only on written request, minimum 5. WT-6 and WT-7 must be filed electronically unless waiver; DOR re-evaluates filing frequency each November and notifies in writing. Tax year 2026: WT-7, W-2 and 1099-R with WI withholding due February 1, 2027. WT-4 copies to DOR when 10+ exemptions or exempt claim with wages over 200/week. Lock-in letters bind employer. 2026 transportation exclusion 340/month parking and 340/month transit/vanpool for federal and WI; 2027 not yet published. PSPs must register and test software; employer stays liable.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. 134.98 Notice of unauthorized acquisition of personal information (ch. 134 published 10-15-25, Wayback copy)
figure_or_rule_carried: Personal information = name linked to SSN, driver licence/state ID, financial account number with access code, DNA profile or biometric data, if not encrypted/redacted. Entity whose personal information is acquired without authorization notifies the subjects within a reasonable time not exceeding 45 days, by mail or a previously used method. Keyword scan of ch. 134: the only 'social security number' hit is the breach definition; no Wisconsin statute located that restricts SSN on pay statements (W-2 employee copy may truncate per DOR, US-WIS5-012). Edition is 10-15-25 (direct docs.legis fetch timed out; Wayback 2026 capture).

instrument_name: Wisconsin DWD Unemployment Insurance 2026 Tax Rates (prior rates page) and 2027 Tax Rates page
article_or_section: Schedule D table; New Employer Rates; Taxable wage base
figure_or_rule_carried: Schedule D in effect for 2026 and for 2027 (2027 page https://dwd.wisconsin.gov/ui/employers/taxrates/). Wage base 14,000. Total rates (basic + solvency): payroll under 500,000 from 0.00 (reserve 15%+) to 12.00 (overdrawn 9%+); payroll 500,000+ from 0.05 to 12.00. New employer 3.05 (2.50+0.55) under 500,000 / 3.25 (2.50+0.75) 500,000+; new construction 2.50 / 2.70; 2027 unchanged. Zero-rate employers still file quarterly reports. Basic rates match the statutory Schedule D in 108.18(4) (US-WIS5-014).

instrument_name: Wisconsin DWD Unemployment News for Employers (2026 edition)
article_or_section: Secretary message; Quarterly Reports Mailing Discontinued; Enhanced Employer Portal; Handbook updates
figure_or_rule_carried: 2027 UI rates stay on Schedule D; UI Trust Fund about 2.3 billion on 2026-06-30. DWD stops mailing quarterly reports in 2027 (file electronically in UI Employer Portal). Enhanced UI Employer Portal rolling out fall 2026, MyWisconsin ID login required. UI Employer Handbook update announced for fall 2026 (current edition R. 03/16/2026).

instrument_name: Office of the Governor press release 2026-03-30: 2025 Wisconsin Act 145 (AB 651, worker's compensation) and Act 144 (AB 650, partial veto, UI administration)
authority: State of Wisconsin, Office of the Governor
figure_or_rule_carried: Act 145 (signed 2026-03-30): worker's compensation changes (maximum weekly compensation rate up, PTSD coverage for EMS, penalties for uninsured employers and misclassification to cut premiums); no payroll withholding effect. Act 144: partial veto of AB 650 on DWD UI administration appropriation; no contribution-rate or wage-base change (confirmed by DWD 2026/2027 rate pages, US-WIS5-019). Act texts not read.

instrument_name: Wis. Stat. 103.64-103.82 Employment of minors: 103.70 permits (published 10-1-26)
figure_or_rule_carried: A minor under 16 may not be employed without a written work permit from DWD or a permit officer (exceptions: 12+ in farming, 14+ in youth apprenticeship, household work not part of the employer's business, certain nonprofit chores). No permit rule for ages 16-17 in the text read. Minor minimum wage = 7.25 (104.035(2)); opportunity wage 5.90 for under-20s in first 90 days (US-WIS5-001).

instrument_name: Wisconsin UI Employer Handbook UCB-201-P (R. 03/16/2026), Section 2 Part 2: Employment excluded by statute and by election
figure_or_rule_carried: UI exclusions for all employers: students in credit work-study programmes, student nurses/interns, nonresident aliens on F, J, M, Q visas (and spouse/minor child), certain AmeriCorps, 501(a) non-(c)(3) orgs paying under 50 per quarter. Private employers: agricultural and domestic labour below coverage thresholds, commission-only insurance/real-estate agents, unpaid corporate officers, work entirely outside WI, sole proprietor's parent/spouse/child under 18, direct sellers, certain taxi drivers, full-time students at seasonal camps under 13 weeks (from 2023-01-01). Elective: principal corporate officers with 25%+ ownership (small employers, 108.02(15)(L)).
